﴿He arranges the affair﴾, i.e., He firmly establishes the affair and sends down the decree (qada') and the divine measure (qadar), ﴿from the heaven to the earth﴾. It is also said: He sends down the revelation (wahy) with Jibril from the heaven to the earth. ﴿Then it ascends﴾, i.e., it rises, ﴿to Him﴾, meaning Jibril ascends with the matter, ﴿in a day the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count﴾, i.e., in one day of the days of this world, and the distance covered is a thousand years: five hundred for its descent and five hundred for its ascent, because the distance between the heaven and the earth is five hundred years. It is said: if one of the children of Adam were to travel it, he would not cover it except in a thousand years, whereas the angels cover it in one day. This describes the ascent of the angel from the earth to the heaven. As for His words, "The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years" (al-Ma'arij: 4), it refers to the duration of the distance between the earth and Sidrat al-Muntaha, which is the station of Jibril. Jibril and the angels of his station who are with him travel a distance of fifty thousand years in one day of the days of this world. All of this is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid and al-Dahhak [[See: al-Tabari: 21/91.]]. His words "to Him" mean: to Allah. It is also said that, according to this interpretation, it means: to the place of the angel to which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to ascend.

Some of them said: a thousand years [and fifty thousand years] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]] are all within the Day of Resurrection, and it will be longer for some of them and shorter for others. The meaning is: He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth for the duration of the days of this world. Then it ascends, i.e., the affair and the arrangement return to Him after the passing away of this world and the cessation of the command of rulers and the judgment of judges, in a day the measure of which is a thousand years, and this is the Day of Resurrection. As for His words "fifty thousand years," He intends that for the disbeliever, Allah makes that day last the measure of fifty thousand years, while for the believer it is less than that, until there came in a hadith: "It will be upon the believer like the time of an obligatory prayer that he prayed in the world" [[Imam Ahmad narrated (3/75) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it will be made lighter upon the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in the world." **[74a]** ﴿That is the Knower of the unseen and the seen﴾, meaning: that One who did what was mentioned, namely the creation of the heavens and the earth, knows what is hidden from creation and what is present. ﴿The Mighty, the Merciful﴾.

﴿Who made good everything He created﴾. Nafi' and the people of Kufa read "خَلَقَهُ" (*khalaqahu*) with a fatha on the lam, as a verb. The others read it with a sukun on the lam (*khalqahu*), meaning: He made the creation of everything good. Ibn Abbas said: He perfected it and made it firm. Qatadah said: He made it beautiful. Muqatil said: He knew how to create everything, from your saying, "So-and-so does (yuhsinu) such-and-such," when he knows it. It was also said: He created every animal in its own form and did not create some in the form of others. So every animal is complete in its creation and beautiful, and each of its limbs is measured to what its livelihood requires.

﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾, meaning Adam.

﴿Then He made his offspring﴾, meaning his descendants, ﴿from an extract﴾, a drop (nutfah). It was called *sulalah* because it is extracted (tusallu) from the human being, ﴿from a despised fluid﴾, meaning weak, and it is the drop of the man.

﴿Then He proportioned him﴾, then He proportioned his form, ﴿and breathed into him of His spirit﴾. Then He returned to his descendants and said: ﴿And He made for you﴾, after you were drops, ﴿hearing and sight and hearts﴾, ﴿little are you grateful﴾, meaning: you do not thank the Lord of these blessings so that you might affirm His oneness.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning those who deny the Resurrection, ﴿"When we have gone astray (ḍalalnā) in the earth﴾, meaning we have perished and become dust. Its root is from their saying: "the water went astray (ḍalla) in the milk," when it disappeared. ﴿"Shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾, an interrogative of denial. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾, meaning in the resurrection after death.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 32, verses 11–12:**

﴿Say: "The Angel of Death, who has been entrusted with you, will take your souls."﴾ He seizes your spirits. ﴿The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you﴾ means: he has been entrusted with seizing your spirits, and he is ʿAzrāʾīl. *Tawaffi* (taking in full) means receiving the full number, meaning that he seizes their spirits until none remains of the number for whom death has been decreed. It is related that the world was made available to the Angel of Death like the palm of a hand, from which its owner takes whatever he wishes without difficulty. He seizes the souls of creation in the east and west of the earth, and he has assistants from the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment. [[See: al-Tabari: 21/541.]] Ibn ʿAbbās said: the stride of the Angel of Death is the distance between the east and the west. [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/543 to Abu al-Shaykh from Ibn ʿAbbās as a statement of his own (mawquf).]] Mujahid said: the earth was made for him like a basin (*tast*), from which he takes whatever he wishes. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 21/97–98.]] In some reports: the Angel of Death is on a ladder (*miʿrāj*) between heaven and earth, and his assistants draw out the human spirit; when it reaches his throat, the Angel of Death seizes it.

Khalid ibn Maʿdan narrated from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Angel of Death has a spear that reaches between the east and the west, and he examines the faces of people. There is no household but that the Angel of Death examines them twice every day. When he sees a person whose term has ended, he strikes his head with that spear and says: "Now the army of the dead will be visited through you." His words: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ means: you will return to Him alive, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

﴿And if you could see when the criminals﴾ — the polytheists — ﴿are bowing their heads﴾ — lowering their heads — ﴿before their Lord﴾ out of shame and remorse, ﴿saying: "Our Lord, we have seen﴾ — what we used to deny — ﴿and we have heard﴾ from You the confirmation of what Your messengers brought us. It was also said: we have seen our disobedience and heard what was said about us. ﴿So send us back﴾ — return us to the world — ﴿that we may do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain.﴾ The answer to *law* (if) is omitted; its implied meaning is: "you would have seen a marvel."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 17:

﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them﴾. Hamzah and Ya'qub recited "أُخْفِي لَهُمْ" (*ukhfiya lahum*) with a sukun on the yā' (ending it with a silent, rather than vowelled, letter), meaning: "I hide it for them." The evidence for this reading (*ḥujjah*, the supporting argument) is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, "نُخْفِي" (*nukhfī*) with a nūn. The others recited it with a fatḥah on the yā'.

﴿from that which is a delight for their eyes﴾: that with which their eyes are gladdened, ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Malīḥī, who said: we were informed by Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, who said: we were informed by Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said: we were informed by Isḥāq ibn Naṣr, who said: we were informed by Abū Usāmah, from al-Aʿmash, who said: we were informed by Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, blessed and exalted, says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as a treasure, let alone what you have been shown of it." Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "This is among the things that have no tafsīr (explanation)." And from some of them it is reported that he said: "They hid their deeds, so Allah hid their reward."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 18–20:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.﴾ It was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it, the half-brother of Uthman through their mother. The reason was that a dispute and an exchange of words arose between them over something. Al-Walid ibn Uqba said to Ali, "Be quiet, for you are a child, and by God, I am more eloquent of tongue than you, sharper of spear than you, braver of heart than you, and fuller in filling the ranks of the battalion than you." Ali said to him, "Be quiet, for you are a fasiq (defiantly disobedient wrongdoer)." So God Most High revealed: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.⁠﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 21/107; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 405–406; and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/553.]] He did not say "they two are not equal" (la yastawiyan), because He did not intend one believer and one fasiq, but rather He intended all the believers and all the fasiqun.

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the gardens of refuge (jannat al-ma'wa)﴾, which the believers take as their refuge, ﴿as a welcome (nuzul) for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And as for those who were defiantly disobedient, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to come out of it, they will be returned into it, and it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾
